rules.fix: Matching instruction to a student's preferred 'learning style' has no supporting evidence (Pashler et al., 2008). Match the medium to the content instead.
Some functions are lateralised, but people are not 'left-brained' or 'right-brained' (Nielsen et al., 2013).
Imaging shows virtually all of the brain is active over a day; there is no dormant 90%.
The 1993 'Mozart effect' was a small, short-lived arousal effect on one spatial task; it does not raise IQ.
Humans have many more senses than five (balance, proprioception, temperature, pain, interoception...).
All taste qualities are detected across the whole tongue; the 'tongue map' came from a mistranslation of Hänig (1901).
Human blood is always red (darker when deoxygenated). Veins look blue because of how skin scatters and absorbs light.
Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor (~6–7 Mya); neither descended from the other.
'Fitness' means reproductive success in an environment, not strength.
A scientific theory is a well-tested explanatory framework, not a guess.
Goldfish retain trained associations for months.
All bats can see; many also echolocate.
Skin dehydrates and retracts after death; hair and nails do not grow.
Controlled trials find no effect of sugar on children's behaviour (Wolraich et al., 1995).
Cattle are red–green colour-blind; bulls react to the cape's motion.
Seasons are caused by axial tilt (23.4°). Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January.
Air over the top of a wing arrives at the trailing edge *before* the air underneath; lift comes from the wing turning the flow (pressure difference ↔ downwash), not equal transit times.
Without air resistance all objects fall with the same acceleration (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²).
Glass is an amorphous solid; medieval panes are uneven because of how they were made, not because they flowed.
Electron drift velocity in a wire is ~mm/s; the *signal* (the electromagnetic field) propagates near light speed.
Current is the same in and out of a series component; energy (not charge) is transferred.
Rubbing transfers electrons between materials; charge is conserved, not created.
Current divides among *all* parallel paths, inversely to their resistance; most, not all, takes the lowest-resistance path.
Heat is energy transfer; *warm fluid* rises because it is less dense (convection). Heat also conducts and radiates downward.

In an inertial frame there is no outward force: objects tend to continue straight and the inward (centripetal) force is missing. 'Centrifugal' is a rotating-frame fictitious force; say which frame you mean.
Gravity on the ISS is ~90% of surface gravity; astronauts float because they are in continuous free fall.
Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium; it cannot travel through a vacuum.
The Sun shines by nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium, not combustion (there is no oxygen burning).
Phases are the changing view of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits; Earth's shadow causes *eclipses*.
The far side gets as much sunlight as the near side; it's only 'dark' in the sense of unseen from Earth.
Polaris is ~48th brightest; Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.
A light-year is a distance (~9.46 × 10¹² km).
Venus is the hottest planet (~465 °C) because of its CO₂ greenhouse atmosphere.
Far from a black hole its gravity is the same as any object of equal mass; it doesn't 'suck'.
Small raindrops are spherical; larger ones flatten into a hamburger-bun shape.
The sky is blue because air molecules scatter short wavelengths more (Rayleigh scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴).
Coriolis effects are far too weak to set the swirl direction of a sink or toilet; basin shape and residual motion dominate.
Lightning often strikes the same tall object repeatedly (the Empire State Building is hit ~20–25 times a year).
A penny's terminal velocity (~25–50 mph) is far too low to kill.
The Mpemba effect is real in some setups but disputed and not reproducible in general; present it as an open question.
Most natural diamonds form ~150 km down in the mantle, from carbon that was never coal.
Pure water is a poor conductor; dissolved ions make ordinary water conductive.
The ozone hole and greenhouse warming are distinct problems with different causes (CFCs vs. CO₂ and other GHGs).
Non-avian dinosaurs went extinct ~66 Mya; the genus Homo appears ~2.8 Mya.
The planetary picture is the 1913 Bohr model. Present it as historical; electrons occupy orbitals described by quantum mechanics.
π is irrational; 22/7 ≈ 3.142857 is an approximation (π ≈ 3.141593).
Division by zero is undefined in the real numbers; limits like 1/x as x→0⁺ grow without bound, which is a different statement.
Golden-ratio claims about the Parthenon, Mona Lisa, pyramids and nautilus shells are largely unsupported (Markowsky, 1992); nautilus spirals are logarithmic but not golden.
The relationship a²+b²=c² was used in Babylon (Plimpton 322, c. 1800 BCE) and elsewhere long before Pythagoras; the first surviving *proof* is in Euclid.
The sequence appears in Indian prosody (Pingala, Virahāṅka, Hemacandra) centuries before Leonardo of Pisa popularised it in Europe (1202).
The place-value digits were developed in India and transmitted to Europe through Arabic scholars (al-Khwārizmī); call them Hindu–Arabic numerals.
Educated Europeans had known Earth was a sphere since antiquity (Eratosthenes measured it c. 240 BCE). Columbus's dispute was about Earth's *size* — and he was wrong.
Einstein excelled at mathematics and had mastered calculus by about 15.
Newton's own account (via Stukeley) is of seeing an apple fall in the orchard; it didn't hit his head.
The Pisa drop is attested only by Galileo's late biographer Viviani and may never have happened; Galileo's documented evidence came from inclined-plane experiments.
Incandescent lamps predate Edison (Davy, de la Rue, Swan). Edison's team produced a practical long-life carbon-filament bulb and, crucially, a distribution system (1879–82).
Newcomen's atmospheric engine (1712) came first; Watt's separate condenser (1765, patented 1769) made it far more efficient.
Movable type existed in China (Bi Sheng, c. 1040) and Korea (Jikji, 1377). Gutenberg (c. 1450) combined metal type, oil-based ink and a screw press into a scalable system.
Franklin's kite was not struck directly (that would likely have killed him, as it did Georg Richmann in 1753); it collected charge from the storm cloud's field.
'First computer' depends on definition (programmable? electronic? stored-program?). Name the criterion: e.g., Z3 1941, Colossus 1943–44, ENIAC 1945, Manchester Baby 1948.
Excavations at Giza (Lehner, Hawass) indicate paid, fed, rotating crews of Egyptian labourers, not chattel slaves.
No Viking-age horned helmet has been found; the image comes from 19th-century Romanticism (Wagner costumes, 1876).
Napoleon was about 1.69 m (5′7″), average for his time; the myth mixes French and English inches.
No one was burned in the Salem trials (1692); 19 were hanged and Giles Corey was pressed to death.
A vomitorium is an amphitheatre exit passage that 'spews out' crowds; it was not a room for vomiting.
There is no evidence Marie Antoinette said it; Rousseau attributes a similar line to 'a great princess' in a text written when she was a child.
Most historians avoid 'Dark Ages' for the early Middle Ages; use 'early medieval period' and acknowledge its scholarship (e.g., Islamic Golden Age, Carolingian renaissance).
Since the IAU's 2006 definition, the Solar System has eight planets; Pluto is a dwarf planet.
The 'insanity is doing the same thing…' line is not found in Einstein's writings; its earliest known appearance is 1980s recovery literature.
There is no evidence Henry Ford said 'if I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses.'
